title: RepoHone session record (V1)
description: One record per coding-agent session, per checkout. Machine-readable shape only: ARCHITECTURE.md owns the semantics, and this schema implements them without redefining them. Capture writes this record during the session; reconciliation fills its phase-two fields later. Analysis output — correction classes, fingerprints, suppression findings, diagnoses — lives in separate records keyed by (session_id, checkout_id), so a session record stays immutable evidence.

schema_version.description: How this JSON record is shaped. A reader that does not support this value must fail clearly or skip explicitly; it must never guess field semantics. Incompatible changes produce session-record.v2.schema.json.

contract_version.description: Which ARCHITECTURE.md semantic interpretation produced this record. A supported shape carrying unsupported newer semantics must refuse semantic analysis unless an explicit migration exists.

session_id.description: RepoHone session identity, derived as rh_ + stable_hash(host, host_session_id) so independent hooks compute it without coordination. This is the id session-sensitive tools take. It is NOT the agent-native id — see host.session_id.

name.description: Coding agent host, e.g. claude-code or codex.

session_id.description: Agent-native session identifier, as supplied by the host.

state.description: observed = captured but the branch/PR outcome is not yet resolved; reconciled = outcome resolved. A session that ends without reconciliation stays observed — that is normal, not an error. Whether the host signalled session end is carried by ended_at and end_reason, not by a separate state.

ended_at.description: Set when the host signalled session end. Null means the session was never cleanly closed.

starts.description: Every session-start seen (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork). More than one entry means the session was resumed or restarted.

adapter.description: Host adapter that produced this record.

content_policy.description: redacted = text stored after secret redaction; hash_only = only hashes and lengths stored.

cwds.description: Every repository root this record saw events from. A different root means a different store, so the session is split across records; join those on (session_id, turns[].logical_turn_id).

errors.description: Capture failures that degraded this record rather than losing it. Bounded to the most recent entries.

models.description: Session-level model observations in order; a model applies from from_turn until the next observation. Model identity is recorded only when the host exposes it reliably — unobserved is valid and is represented by an empty array and null turns[].model. Model segmentation is a confounder-control dimension applied to sessions with known identity, not a prerequisite for any metric. Prefer turns[].model, which is observed per turn.

id.description: Pseudonymous identifier (hash of the configured commit email). Used only to distinguish shared invariants from individual preference.

root.description: Absolute local path; machine-specific and not an identity.

id.description: Logical repository identity — hash of the normalised origin remote, identical for ssh and https forms. Joins records for one repository across checkouts and machines. Null when there is no origin remote.

checkout_id.description: Identity of this specific working copy. Mutable telemetry is checkout-scoped and destructive operations act on it, so it must travel with the record: neither storage location nor root path survives export or aggregation.

branches_observed.description: Every branch seen in any snapshot. Used by reconciliation to map session -> branch -> PR (many-to-one).

turns.description: One entry per logical turn, identified by the host's logical_turn_id. A turn holds every prompt event and every stop event belonging to it, each with its own snapshot, because a turn may receive several prompt submissions (type-ahead) and several stop events.

session_end_snapshots.description: Snapshot taken at each session end. A difference from the last stop event's snapshot means files changed after the agent's last turn but before the session closed. Every entry is a session_end-class snapshot.

stored_path.description: Redacted, gzipped copy. Null under hash_only policy, when copying is disabled, or when the session never closed cleanly.

developer_label.description: Optional human ground truth. null = not yet labelled; NONE = labelled as containing no correction. Canonical enum: LEARNING_PLAN.md references this definition rather than restating it.

resolution.description: Which state reconciliation treats as the agent's final output. Provisional until confirmed: a stop event alone never proves finality, and an interrupted or failed turn proves less.

accepted_snapshot.description: Merged tree. Post-session correction evidence = diff(agent_final_snapshot.snapshot.tree, accepted_snapshot.tree), restricted to agent-touched and related files. Compare trees, never commit ancestry: rebases and squash merges break ancestry.

related_session_ids.description: Other RepoHone sessions that contributed to the same PR.

extensions.description: Experimental fields. Anything that becomes load-bearing must move into a new schema version.

ref.description: Local git ref. Never branch history, never pushed by push/--all/--tags.

class.description: Snapshot class. The ref encodes it too, but analysis must not have to parse ref strings.

ordinal.description: Atomically allocated from RepoHone's local state, never derived by counting refs, never reused after a ref is deleted. Append-only: a new event never overwrites an earlier one.

path.description: Null at the repository root; otherwise this submodule's path relative to its parent. The ref and objects live in that submodule's own object store.

submodules.description: A parent tree records a submodule only as a gitlink, so working-tree edits inside one are invisible there. Each initialised submodule is snapshotted separately; a turn's diff is the parent trees plus each submodule's trees, matched by path.

text.description: Redacted text, or null under hash_only policy.

ordinal.description: 1 is the turn's baseline and is immutable; later ordinals are additional submissions.

snapshot.description: Stable working-tree state observed when this submission was received, over the captured file set. Null when no stable state could be captured; capture.errors then says why.

kind.description: stop = the agent concluded the turn; stop_failure = an API error ended it.

error.description: Host error class for stop_failure (rate_limit, overloaded, max_output_tokens, ...). Turns ended by infrastructure error must be excluded from correction rates rather than counted as agent output. Null for kind=stop, and null on hosts that report no equivalent.

snapshot.description: Stable working-tree state observed by RepoHone during this lifecycle event. It is NOT guaranteed to precede sibling hooks: hooks on one event run concurrently, so a project-native verification hook may already be running. Capture retries on concurrent mutation of the captured file set and, failing to obtain a stable state, writes null plus a capture.errors entry rather than recording a mixed tree as authoritative evidence.

effort.description: Effort level reported by the host for this event, where exposed.

model.description: Model identity for this event where the host exposes it reliably; null otherwise, never inferred.

host_continuation.description: Host continuation metadata (stop_hook_active): true means this event follows a hook asking the agent to continue. Recorded as host metadata only; RepoHone never uses it as an event ordinal.

index.description: Position within this record only. Join across record fragments on logical_turn_id.

logical_turn_id.description: The host's identity for one user turn, supplied by the adapter — prompt_id on Claude Code, turn_id on Codex. Stable across repeated stop events, so it is the join key, never an event counter. Required: an adapter whose host cannot supply one must derive a deterministic equivalent or disable turn-dependent capture. It must never write an ambiguous record, because the joins this schema relies on would silently break.

prompt_events.description: Every prompt submission belonging to this turn, append-only. More than one means the developer typed ahead while the agent was working and the host merged the submissions into one turn; a queued follow-up is itself correction evidence. Empty only for a turn opened by a stop event with no captured prompt.

stop_events.description: Every stop event belonging to this turn, append-only, each with its own snapshot. More than one occurs when something asks the agent to continue. Empty means the turn never reached a stop: still running, interrupted, or the session died mid-turn.

workspace_changed_before_turn.description: True if the tree at prompt_events[0] differs from the previous turn's last stop event snapshot — evidence that source changed outside the agent's previous cycle. Null for the first turn, when a snapshot is missing, or when the previous turn never reached a stop, because an interrupted turn has no moment at which the agent stopped and nothing is attributable. Does not by itself prove a human edit.

completion.description: stop = the agent concluded; stop_failure = an API error ended it; interrupted = the developer stopped it, so no stop event ever fired; pending = still running, or the session died mid-turn.

completion_source.description: observed = a host event reported this completion. derived = inferred, because on some hosts an interrupted turn is observable only as an absence and is closed at the next snapshot. Which applies to an interruption is host-specific and belongs to the adapter; stop and stop_failure are always observed. Analysis must never treat a derived boundary as an observed one.

model.description: Model that produced this turn where reliably exposed; null otherwise. Never inferred from heuristics to enable segmentation.
